cards.text: Paul the apostle is writing to the church in Corinth. He preaches that Christ has been raised from the dead. But some of them are saying something that doesn't fit with that at ALL.

cards.question: What are some people in Corinth saying that clashes with Christ being raised?

answers.text: There is no resurrection of the dead
Paul is not a real apostle

cards.text: So Paul grabs that idea and follows it all the way out. It's like pulling one loose thread on a sweater, friend. You keep pulling and watch what comes apart.

cards.question: Paul says that even if there's no resurrection of the dead, Christ could still have been raised.

cards.text: Paul keeps pulling that thread. If Christ has not been raised, two things become worthless right along with it.

cards.question: Paul says if Christ has not been raised, the apostles' ___ is worthless, and so is the Corinthians' ___.

cards.text: Now it gets personal for Paul. He and the others have testified about God that He raised Christ from the dead.

cards.question: If the dead are not raised, Paul says that exposes him and the others as what?

cards.text: Picture giving the whole town directions to a house that isn't there. Every single person you sent is coming back looking for YOU.
Then Paul circles back to his main point: if the dead are not raised, then not even Christ has been raised. And this time he says what that means for the Corinthians themselves.

cards.question: If Christ has not been raised, Paul tells the Corinthians their faith is ___.
And if Christ wasn't raised, where does Paul say that leaves the Corinthians?

cards.text: Then Paul thinks about the believers who have already died. He calls them those who have fallen asleep in Christ.

cards.question: If Christ wasn't raised, Paul says those who have fallen asleep in Christ are simply resting safely.

cards.text: Then Paul zooms way out. What if their whole hope in Christ is only for this life?

cards.question: What does Paul say about believers if their hope in Christ is for this life alone?

answers.text: They should be pitied more than anyone
They should be envied more than anyone
They should be feared more than anyone

cards.text: Friend, Paul walked us right up to the edge of the cliff just so he could say this: "But Christ has indeed been raised from the dead." SOMEBODY get this man a microphone!

cards.question: Paul calls the risen Christ the firstfruits of those who have fallen asleep. What does that picture point to?

answers.text: He is the first of many to be raised
He is the only one ever to be raised
He was the first person ever to die

cards.text: Paul explains how it all works. Death came through a man.

cards.question: So how does Paul say the resurrection of the dead comes?
Paul says in ___ all die, and in ___ all will be made alive.

cards.text: But it doesn't all happen at once: each in his own turn. Like take-a-number tickets at the DMV, everybody gets called, just not all at the same time.

cards.question: Christ goes first as the firstfruits. Who does Paul say comes next?

answers.text: Those who belong to Him at His coming
Everyone on earth the very next day

cards.text: Then the end will come. Christ destroys all dominion, authority and power, and hands over the kingdom to God the Father.

cards.question: Paul says Christ must reign until something happens. Until what?

answers.text: Until all His enemies are under His feet
Until the temple is rebuilt in Jerusalem
Until the last apostle has died

cards.question: Paul names the very last enemy to be destroyed. What is it?

cards.text: DEATH. Last enemy on the list, and Paul says it's getting destroyed. Friend, I'm standing on my gold base CLAPPING with my mustache.
Paul quotes Scripture: "God has put everything under His feet." Then he points out the obvious: everything doesn't include God, the One who put everything under Him.

cards.question: When all things are subjected to Him, the Son Himself will be made subject to God. Why?

answers.text: So that God may be all in all
So that the Son can begin His reign
So that the angels can rule the earth

cards.text: Paul comes at it from another angle. He points to people who are baptized for the dead.

cards.question: What question does Paul raise about people being baptized for the dead?

answers.text: Why do it if the dead are never raised
Who gave them permission to do it
Why did they wait so long to do it

cards.text: Then Paul turns it on himself and the others. Why would they put themselves in danger every hour?

cards.question: How often does Paul tell the Corinthians he faces death?

cards.text: Me? I held my breath every time a drawer opened. Paul faces death EVERY. SINGLE. DAY. and then asks, "If I fought wild beasts in Ephesus for human motives, what did I gain?"

cards.question: If the dead are not raised, what way of living does Paul say might as well take over?

answers.text: Live it up since tomorrow we die
Work hard since the end is near
Stay quiet since no one is listening

cards.question: Paul warns the Corinthians not to be deceived. What does he say bad company does to good character?

cards.text: Then Paul gives them a wake-up call. Sober up as you ought, and stop sinning.

cards.question: Why does Paul tell the Corinthians to sober up and stop sinning?

answers.text: Some of them are ignorant of God
Some of them are leaving the church
Some of them are too proud to pray

cards.text: Paul says all this to their shame. But don't close the cookie box yet, friend. He's not finished teaching on this.

findings.problem: Stop 2, card 1 quotes "But Christ has indeed been raised from the dead.", which isn't the exact BSB wording.

rule.text: Quotes: Quotation marks around Bible words mean the exact BSB wording, punctuation included.

findings.problem: The opening card uses facts from outside the passage without citing them. It says Paul is writing to the church in Corinth (1 Corinthians 1:1-2) and that Paul preaches Christ raised (15:11). Verse 12 only says 'if it is preached.' The card cites only 1 Corinthians 15:12.

rule.text: Facts from outside the passage are fine when they help, like who a new person is or who wrote a letter, with their reference.

findings.problem: The card cites 1 Corinthians 15:13 but tells nothing from that verse. It only says Paul follows the idea out, plus the sweater joke. Verse 13's content first appears on choice card 4.

rule.text: Cite exactly what the card uses. Every story card cites the verses it tells, from the first verse it uses to the last, no wider and no narrower.

findings.problem: The wrong answers 'money', 'homes' and 'names' are not the same kind of thing as 'preaching' and 'faith'. They sound off-topic, so the two right answers stand out as the only ones that fit Paul's argument.

rule.text: Don't let the right answer stand out. All the answers should sound alike. None should sound more like the Bible, or more modern, than the others.

findings.problem: The question asks what being 'exposed' makes them. 'Exposes' signals something negative, so 'Faithful servants of God' and 'Chosen prophets of God' are ruled out by the wording. Both wrong answers are positive and the right answer is the only negative one.

rule.text: A setup line can't rule out the wrong answers either.

findings.problem: This story card is only a joke. It tells no part of 1 Corinthians 15:15, yet cites 15:15. It does not move the passage forward.

rule.text: Every story card tells part of the passage. Jokes ride along on those cards.

findings.problem: The card says 'this time he says what that means for the Corinthians themselves'. That implies this is the first time Paul applies it to them. But verse 14 already said 'and so is your faith.'

rule.text: Noticing: What he points out must be true.

findings.problem: The setup is about everything collapsing if Christ wasn't raised. Both wrong answers, 'Free from the law' and 'Safe from all judgment', are good outcomes, so the setup rules them out. 'Still in their sins' is the only answer that fits.

rule.text: A setup line can't rule out the wrong answers either.

findings.problem: The card says 'their whole hope in Christ', but verse 19 says 'our hope' and 'we are to be pitied'. Paul includes himself. The retelling changes who the text is about.

rule.text: Call things what the text calls them.

findings.problem: 'Paul walked us right up to the edge of the cliff just so he could say this' adds a reason for why Paul argued verses 12-19. The text doesn't state that reason.

rule.text: Reasons: He never adds why someone did, said or thought something unless the text says why.

findings.problem: The right answer 'He is the first of many to be raised' interprets 'firstfruits' as 'first to be raised'. Elsewhere in Scripture, people were raised from the dead before Christ, such as Lazarus (John 11) and the widow's son (1 Kings 17). The 'of many' part also comes from verse 23, but the card cites only 15:20.
findings.question: For a meaning question about an image like 'firstfruits', may the right answer state an interpretation that other passages seem to complicate? Should the citation include verses outside the asked verse that support it?

findings.problem: Multiple choice dominates the stop: 6 of 7 choice cards are multiple choice and only 1 is fill in the blank. There are no true or false cards.

rule.text: No formula. Which question type comes next, the order the types come in and where a blank falls are chosen naturally for each card. They never follow a pattern. No stop repeats another stop's pattern, and no type dominates a stop by a wide margin.

findings.problem: The card restates verse 26, which choice card 10 just answered ('Last enemy on the list, and Paul says it's getting destroyed'), plus a reaction joke. It is a recap and does not move the passage forward.
The card says 'Paul quotes Scripture' but gives no reference for the quoted Scripture (Psalm 8:6).

rule.text: References. Every Bible fact he states carries its reference.

findings.problem: The question opens 'When all things are subjected to Him' without saying who 'Him' is. The baker can't see the earlier card, and the pronoun could be read as God rather than the Son.

rule.text: Always give context in the question. The story card before it isn't on screen anymore, so the question says who and what. Never "him," "that" or "it" pointing back to a card the baker can't see.

findings.problem: All 5 choice cards in the stop are multiple choice. One type completely dominates the stop.

rule.text: No formula. Which question type comes next, the order the types come in and where a blank falls are chosen naturally for each card. They never follow a pattern. No stop repeats another stop's pattern, and no type dominates a stop by a wide margin.

findings.problem: 'I held my breath every time a drawer opened' leans on a drawer detail the baker hasn't been told: the fear of being thrown out when the drawer opened. Without that setup, a stranger would ask why he held his breath.

rule.text: A callback only works if its setup came earlier in this lesson or conversation.

findings.problem: The question already says 'bad company' and that Paul warns them 'not to be deceived'. That rules out 'It protects it' and 'It sharpens it', so no reasoning is needed.

rule.text: A setup line can't rule out the wrong answers either.

findings.problem: 'Paul says all this to their shame' widens the text. Verse 34 says 'I say this to your shame,' which doesn't say it covers everything in the passage.

rule.text: Don't stretch the text. Exaggerate only in his own jokes.
